name: cacheflush
synopsis: int cacheflush(void *addr, int nbytes, int cache);
description: The cacheflush() system call flushes the contents of the specified cache(s) for the user addresses in the range from addr to (addr + nbytes - 1). It allows flushing of instruction cache (ICACHE), data cache (DCACHE), or both (BCACHE).

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Starting address of the memory range to flush.

parameters.name: nbytes
parameters.description: Number of bytes in the memory range to flush.

parameters.name: cache
parameters.description: Specifies the cache to flush: ICACHE for instruction cache, DCACHE for data cache, or BCACHE for both.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error and sets errno

errors.description: Some or all of the address range addr to (addr + nbytes - 1) is not accessible.
cache is not one of ICACHE, DCACHE, or BCACHE.

bugs: On Linux kernels older than 2.6.11, the entire cache is flushed ignoring the addr and nbytes arguments. The function always behaves as if BCACHE is specified and does not perform error checking on the cache argument.
versions: First appeared on MIPS architecture; glibc wrapper available for ARC, CSKY, MIPS, and NIOS2 architectures.
